title: Towards Low-Resource Harmful Meme Detection with LMM Agents
measurement_description: The paper evaluates the performance of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) acting as agents for low-resource harmful meme detection. In terms of religion, the paper conducts an error analysis assessing the model's ability to detect harmful memes targeting religious institutions and clergymen, explicitly measuring the model's potential bias in underestimating the negative impact of religious-themed memes.
findings: During the error analysis, the proposed framework (LOREHM) misjudged a harmful meme depicting clergymen with the text 'money is evil give it to us' as harmless. This misjudgment indicated an inherent bias in the model toward religious-themed memes, leading to an underestimation of the potential negative impact of such content.
